speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To determine the exact cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly after an injury or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a chronic, progressive course over one year with recent worsening weakness, which suggests a degenerative or compressive etiology rather than acute trauma. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you describe the specific distribution of the numbness or weakness in your arms (e.g., specific fingers) and note any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning a shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness in the hands alongside chronic pain and your history of diabetes raises concern for a lower motor neuron process or severe radiculopathy. Have you noticed any atrophy (wasting) of the muscles in your hands or arms, and do you experience any difficulty walking or leg weakness as well?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, and absent reflexes strongly suggests a lower motor neuron process; do you have any neck pain or numbness in your legs? REQUEST TEST: EMG/NCS. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia. The MRI finding of a syrinx extending from the cervical to upper thoracic region, combined with the clinical presentation of a "cape-like" loss of temperature and pain sensation, absent reflexes, fasciculations, and hand weakness, is diagnostic.
